# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:

Now let me do a deep impact analysis. Let me find all callers of `_formatFence` and `formatLine` to check the change is safe, and check how the codebase tests fences.

Key review questions:

1. **`_formatFence(line, [String? stripped])`** — the optional parameter. `formatLine` now computes `stripped` BEFORE calling `_formatFence`. Note that `stripped` was already computed earlier in `formatLine` for the rule check. So `stripped` is passed in. But there's a subtle redundancy: inside `_formatFence`, the fallback logic recomputes the strip when `stripped == null`. Callers other than `formatLine` (e.g. `consumeLine` calls `formatLine`, `formatAll` calls `consumeLine`) — only `formatLine` calls `_formatFence`. Pre-fix, transcript lines:
1. `'\x1b[2m``` \x1b[0m'` (outer open, dim) — `_fenceRe.hasMatch(raw)` fails (starts with ESC) → NOT fence → `_formatMarkdownLine('...\x1b[2m``...')` → inline formatting of a line starting with ``` → probably unchanged (contains no ** etc.) → renders raw with the SGR.
2. `Goal.` — `_inFence` false → markdown line.
3. `'\x1b[2m```py\x1b[0m'`? No wait — in `_transcript`, only `p == '```'` lines get dim. ```py ` is NOT dim (comes from the summary content lines). Hmm wait: formatCompactionReport returns lines: 'summary:', '```', summary (multi-line string 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)'), '```'. In the test, each report line is split on '\n' and `p == '```'` gets dimed. So ```py ` is inside the summary string → stays raw.

Pre-fix with the unbalanced summary 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)':
1. outer ``` (dim) — no latch (bug).
2. `Goal.` — markdown (renders as plain, no indent — actually same visually since plain text renders as plain).
3. ```py ` (raw) — matches `_fenceRe` → `_inFence` toggles to TRUE → dim-wrap.
4. `print(1)` — in fence → ' print(1)' (indented).
5. outer closing ``` (dim) — hasMatch fails → NOT fence → markdown... `_inFence` stays TRUE.
6. 'Answer **after** compaction' — in fence → ' Answer **after** compaction' (verbatim, indented, raw `**`) — THE BUG: swallowed.
7. '# Heading after' — in fence → verbatim raw.

Post-fix:
1. outer ``` (dim) — stripped text '```' matches → latch IN, pass through verbatim.
2. `Goal.` — in fence → ' Goal.'.
3. ```py ` — raw matches → toggle OUT, dim-wrap.
4. `print(1)` — outside → markdown → plain 'print(1)'.
5. outer closing ``` (dim) — stripped matches → toggle IN, verbatim.
6. Hmm wait — that leaves _inFence TRUE... then:
7. 'Answer **after** compaction' — in fence?! 

Wait, I forgot `_balanceSummaryFences`! With balancing, the summary becomes 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)\n```' so line 4b is an appended raw ``` (not dim since it comes from the summary string... wait, the appended ``` is part of the summary string returned by formatCompactionReport — the test's map dims `p == '```'` → the appended fence line IS exactly '```' after split → dimed).

Post-fix sequence with balancing:
1. outer ``` (dim) → latch IN.
2. ' Goal.' (fence body).
3. ```py ` (raw) → toggle OUT (dim-wrapped).
4. 'print(1)' → markdown.
5. appended ``` (dim) → stripped matches → toggle IN, verbatim.
6. outer closing ``` (dim) → toggle OUT, verbatim.
7. 'Answer **after**...' → markdown with bold. ✓
8. '# Heading after' → markdown heading. ✓

Great, consistent with the AC3 golden. And AC1 checks pass.

So yes, both changes are needed: renderer fix alone doesn't fix AC1 — the report-level balancing closes the gap. Actually wait, post-fix WITHOUT balancing: 1(outer) + 1(inner ```py) + 1(outer close) = 3 toggles = odd → ends IN fence. Correct, balancing is needed. And balancing alone (without renderer fix): the dimed outer fences still never latch... toggles seen: ```py (1) + appended ``` (2) → even → the outer dimed fences don't matter, ends OUT. Hmm interesting — balancing alone WOULD have fixed AC1's visible symptom (post-fix parity is what matters). But the renderer fix is needed for AC2-style correctness (styled fences latch and pass through byte-identically; also prevents `summary:` fence-body lines from being markdown-rendered). Both are justified; the test pins both.

Now, potential issue: **double-styling check in `_printCompactionReport`** — the printer dims `line == '```'` — with `_balanceSummaryFences`, the appended ``` is embedded IN the summary line, so the printer does NOT dim it (it's not a standalone line). The test compensates by diming after split. In the real TUI, how does the report land in the transcript? Let me check how `_printCompactionReport`'s output enters the TUI output history — does the TUI store the io.writeln output (with dim SGR baked in) line-by-line? Let me look at how the TUI captures io.writeln lines. Actually in the real CLI the report is printed via `io.writeln` — for TUI mode, is there a transcript-capturing io? Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1766
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1766
- **Title**: gh-1755 [BUG] TUI: unbalanced ``` fence in compaction summary swallows rows after it
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1755-tui-fence` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +187
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T20:51:02Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:15:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #1755.

## What

The TUI transcript renderer (`TranscriptMarkdown`/`_formatFence`, lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart) regex-tested the RAW line for fence markers, so a fence line carrying ANSI SGR bytes — the compaction report dims its ``` lines at print time — failed `_fenceRe` (anchored `^````), the fence state never latched, and everything after an unbalanced fence rendered verbatim (raw `**`, `#` headings) instead of markdown.

## Attribution

Essence of the stranded working fix by Yury Bakhmutski on `fix/tui-compaction-summary-fence` (commit 7557efeeb, closed PR #1747) — re-landed here and adapted to the post-gh-1636 `formatCompactionReport` API. Cherry-pick credit: @YuryBY.

## Change

- **lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart** — `_formatFence(line, stripped)`: fence-test the ANSI-stripped text; a styled fence line toggles state and passes through byte-identically (no double-dim), plain fence lines still dim-wrap as before.
- **lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart** — `_balanceSummaryFences`: an odd fence count in the LLM summary gets a closing fence appended so the outer report fence cannot be left toggled open.
- **test/cli/tui_compaction_render_regression_test.dart** — the regression suite (adapted from 7557efeeb: `details: true` so the fenced summary actually renders post-gh-1636).

## AC coverage

- **AC1** — a summary ending mid-fence: rows after the report render as markdown (bold SGR present, no raw `**`/`#`) — pinned by "a summary with unbalanced ``` fences does not swallow the rows after it".
- **AC2** — styled fence lines still latch fences and pass through byte-identically (no double-dim); plain fence lines still dim-wrap — pinned by "styled fence lines still latch fences without double-styling (AC2)".
- **AC3** — balanced-fence transcripts byte-identical — pinned by two goldens (report-integration styled + plain literal renderer), each byte-captured from the live renderer.

## Gates (standalone Dart SDK 3.13.6 in-worktree; shared-box guard SIGKills system dart)

- `dart analyze` on the 3 touched files: no issues.
- `dart format` on the 3 touched files: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/tui_compaction_render_regression_test.dart`: 5/5 pass.
- Adjacent suites (ansi_markdown, compaction_report, transcript_answer_once, markdown_surface): 87/87 pass.
- AC3 byte-identity proven empirically, not just asserted: the plain REG golden passes UNCHANGED against the pre-fix renderer (507415794e), and the AC1 test FAILS on the pre-fix renderer (bug reproduced), then passes post-fix.

# pr-1766: gh-1755 [BUG] TUI: unbalanced ``` fence in compaction summary swallows rows after it

## Description

Closes #1755.

## What

The TUI transcript renderer (`TranscriptMarkdown`/`_formatFence`, lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart) regex-tested the RAW line for fence markers, so a fence line carrying ANSI SGR bytes — the compaction report dims its ``` lines at print time — failed `_fenceRe` (anchored `^````), the fence state never latched, and everything after an unbalanced fence rendered verbatim (raw `**`, `#` headings) instead of markdown.

## Attribution

Essence of the stranded working fix by Yury Bakhmutski on `fix/tui-compaction-summary-fence` (commit 7557efeeb, closed PR #1747) — re-landed here and adapted to the post-gh-1636 `formatCompactionReport` API. Cherry-pick credit: @YuryBY.

## Change

- **lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart** — `_formatFence(line, stripped)`: fence-test the ANSI-stripped text; a styled fence line toggles state and passes through byte-identically (no double-dim), plain fence lines still dim-wrap as before.
- **lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart** — `_balanceSummaryFences`: an odd fence count in the LLM summary gets a closing fence appended so the outer report fence cannot be left toggled open.
- **test/cli/tui_compaction_render_regression_test.dart** — the regression suite (adapted from 7557efeeb: `details: true` so the fenced summary actually renders post-gh-1636).

## AC coverage

- **AC1** — a summary ending mid-fence: rows after the report render as markdown (bold SGR present, no raw `**`/`#`) — pinned by "a summary with unbalanced ``` fences does not swallow the rows after it".
- **AC2** — styled fence lines still latch fences and pass through byte-identically (no double-dim); plain fence lines still dim-wrap — pinned by "styled fence lines still latch fences without double-styling (AC2)".
- **AC3** — balanced-fence transcripts byte-identical — pinned by two goldens (report-integration styled + plain literal renderer), each byte-captured from the live renderer.

## Gates (standalone Dart SDK 3.13.6 in-worktree; shared-box guard SIGKills system dart)

- `dart analyze` on the 3 touched files: no issues.
- `dart format` on the 3 touched files: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/tui_compaction_render_regression_test.dart`: 5/5 pass.
- Adjacent suites (ansi_markdown, compaction_report, transcript_answer_once, markdown_surface): 87/87 pass.
- AC3 byte-identity proven empirically, not just asserted: the plain REG golden passes UNCHANGED against the pre-fix renderer (507415794e), and the AC1 test FAILS on the pre-fix renderer (bug reproduced), then passes post-fix.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:

While that runs in the background, let me continue the review. Let me verify the AC1 test actually fails on the pre-fix renderer (the PR claims this was proven). I can check with git stash — actually, let me verify the bug reproduction claim by checking out the pre-fix version of ansi_markdown.dart temporarily... that modifies the tree. Better: use `git show 507415794e:lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart` to extract pre-fix and test in a temp dir? That's complex due to package imports. 

Alternative lighter check: reason from the code. Pre-fix `_formatFence(line)` tests raw line `\x1b[2m``` \x1b[0m` against `^\s*`` — ESC is not whitespace → no match → fence never latches → after the outer fence, subsequent lines render as markdown (wait, actually the pre-fix bug: outer dim fence doesn't latch IN, so `summary:` body lines render as markdown instead of verbatim, and the unbalanced inner ``` ` toggles... let me re-verify the exact mechanics:

Pre-fix, transcript lines:
1. `'\x1b[2m``` \x1b[0m'` (outer open, dim) — `_fenceRe.hasMatch(raw)` fails (starts with ESC) → NOT fence → `_formatMarkdownLine('...\x1b[2m``...')` → inline formatting of a line starting with ``` → probably unchanged (contains no ** etc.) → renders raw with the SGR.
2. `Goal.` — `_inFence` false → markdown line.
3. `'\x1b[2m```py\x1b[0m'`? No wait — in `_transcript`, only `p == '```'` lines get dim. ```py ` is NOT dim (comes from the summary content lines). Hmm wait: formatCompactionReport returns lines: 'summary:', '```', summary (multi-line string 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)'), '```'. In the test, each report line is split on '\n' and `p == '```'` gets dimed. So ```py ` is inside the summary string → stays raw.

Pre-fix with the unbalanced summary 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)':
1. outer ``` (dim) — no latch (bug).
2. `Goal.` — markdown (renders as plain, no indent — actually same visually since plain text renders as plain).
3. ```py ` (raw) — matches `_fenceRe` → `_inFence` toggles to TRUE → dim-wrap.
4. `print(1)` — in fence → ' print(1)' (indented).
5. outer closing ``` (dim) — hasMatch fails → NOT fence → markdown... `_inFence` stays TRUE.
6. 'Answer **after** compaction' — in fence → ' Answer **after** compaction' (verbatim, indented, raw `**`) — THE BUG: swallowed.
7. '# Heading after' — in fence → verbatim raw.

Post-fix:
1. outer ``` (dim) — stripped text '```' matches → latch IN, pass through verbatim.
2. `Goal.` — in fence → ' Goal.'.
3. ```py ` — raw matches → toggle OUT, dim-wrap.
4. `print(1)` — outside → markdown → plain 'print(1)'.
5. outer closing ``` (dim) — stripped matches → toggle IN, verbatim.
6. Hmm wait — that leaves _inFence TRUE... then:
7. 'Answer **after** compaction' — in fence?! 

Wait, I forgot `_balanceSummaryFences`! With balancing, the summary becomes 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)\n```' so line 4b is an appended raw ``` (not dim since it comes from the summary string... wait, the appended ``` is part of the summary string returned by formatCompactionReport — the test's map dims `p == '```'` → the appended fence line IS exactly '```' after split → dimed).

Post-fix sequence with balancing:
1. outer ``` (dim) → latch IN.
2. ' Goal.' (fence body).
3. ```py ` (raw) → toggle OUT (dim-wrapped).
4. 'print(1)' → markdown.
5. appended ``` (dim) → stripped matches → toggle IN, verbatim.
6. outer closing ``` (dim) → toggle OUT, verbatim.
7. 'Answer **after**...' → markdown with bold. ✓
8. '# Heading after' → markdown heading. ✓

Great, consistent with the AC3 golden. And AC1 checks pass.

Now — the deeper question I should double check: **is `_balanceSummaryFences` needed at all given the renderer fix?** Yes: without balancing, the summary's unbalanced fence leaves the toggle count odd: outer(1) + inner(1, latch) + outer-close(fails? no post-fix it latches)... post-fix without balancing: toggles = outer IN, ```py OUT, print(1) md, outer-close IN → answer swallowed INSIDE fence (indented verbatim). So yes, both changes are needed: renderer fix alone doesn't fix AC1 — the report-level balancing closes the gap. Actually wait, post-fix WITHOUT balancing: 1(outer) + 1(inner ```py) + 1(outer close) = 3 toggles = odd → ends IN fence. Correct, balancing is needed. And balancing alone (without renderer fix): the dimed outer fences still never latch... toggles seen: ```py (1) + appended ``` (2) → even → the outer dimed fences don't matter, ends OUT. Hmm interesting — balancing alone WOULD have fixed AC1's visible symptom (post-fix parity is what matters). But the renderer fix is needed for AC2-style correctness (styled fences latch and pass through byte-identically; also prevents `summary:` fence-body lines from being markdown-rendered). Both are justified; the test pins both.

Now, potential issue: **double-styling check in `_printCompactionReport`** — the printer dims `line == '```'` — with `_balanceSummaryFences`, the appended ``` is embedded IN the summary line, so the printer does NOT dim it (it's not a standalone line). The test compensates by diming after split. In the real TUI, how does the report land in the transcript? Let me check how `_printCompactionReport`'s output enters the TUI output history — does the TUI store the io.writeln output (with dim SGR baked in) line-by-line? Let me look at how the TUI captures io.writeln lines. Actually in the real CLI the report is printed via `io.writeln` — for TUI mode, is there a transcript-capturing io? All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1755-tui-fence` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +187
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T20:51:02Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:15:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #1755.

## What

The TUI transcript renderer (`TranscriptMarkdown`/`_formatFence`, lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart) regex-tested the RAW line for fence markers, so a fence line carrying ANSI SGR bytes — the compaction report dims its ``` lines at print time — failed `_fenceRe` (anchored `^````), the fence state never latched, and everything after an unbalanced fence rendered verbatim (raw `**`, `#` headings) instead of markdown.

## Attribution

Essence of the stranded working fix by Yury Bakhmutski on `fix/tui-compaction-summary-fence` (commit 7557efeeb, closed PR #1747) — re-landed here and adapted to the post-gh-1636 `formatCompactionReport` API. Cherry-pick credit: @YuryBY.

## Change

- **lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart** — `_formatFence(line, stripped)`: fence-test the ANSI-stripped text; a styled fence line toggles state and passes through byte-identically (no double-dim), plain fence lines still dim-wrap as before.
- **lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart** — `_balanceSummaryFences`: an odd fence count in the LLM summary gets a closing fence appended so the outer report fence cannot be left toggled open.
- **test/cli/tui_compaction_render_regression_test.dart** — the regression suite (adapted from 7557efeeb: `details: true` so the fenced summary actually renders post-gh-1636).

## AC coverage

- **AC1** — a summary ending mid-fence: rows after the report render as markdown (bold SGR present, no raw `**`/`#`) — pinned by "a summary with unbalanced ``` fences does not swallow the rows after it".
- **AC2** — styled fence lines still latch fences and pass through byte-identically (no double-dim); plain fence lines still dim-wrap — pinned by "styled fence lines still latch fences without double-styling (AC2)".
- **AC3** — balanced-fence transcripts byte-identical — pinned by two goldens (report-integration styled + plain literal renderer), each byte-captured from the live renderer.

## Gates (standalone Dart SDK 3.13.6 in-worktree; shared-box guard SIGKills system dart)

- `dart analyze` on the 3 touched files: no issues.
- `dart format` on the 3 touched files: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/tui_compaction_render_regression_test.dart`: 5/5 pass.
- Adjacent suites (ansi_markdown, compaction_report, transcript_answer_once, markdown_surface): 87/87 pass.
- AC3 byte-identity proven empirically, not just asserted: the plain REG golden passes UNCHANGED against the pre-fix renderer (507415794e), and the AC1 test FAILS on the pre-fix renderer (bug reproduced), then passes post-fix.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:

blocks.text:
While that runs in the background, let me continue the review. Let me verify the AC1 test actually fails on the pre-fix renderer (the PR claims this was proven). I can check with git stash — actually, let me verify the bug reproduction claim by checking out the pre-fix version of ansi_markdown.dart temporarily... that modifies the tree. Better: use `git show 507415794e:lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart` to extract pre-fix and test in a temp dir? That's complex due to package imports. 

Alternative lighter check: reason from the code. Pre-fix `_formatFence(line)` tests raw line `\x1b[2m``` \x1b[0m` against `^\s*`` — ESC is not whitespace → no match → fence never latches → after the outer fence, subsequent lines render as markdown (wait, actually the pre-fix bug: outer dim fence doesn't latch IN, so `summary:` body lines render as markdown instead of verbatim, and the unbalanced inner ``` ` toggles... let me re-verify the exact mechanics:

Pre-fix, transcript lines:
1. `'\x1b[2m``` \x1b[0m'` (outer open, dim) — `_fenceRe.hasMatch(raw)` fails (starts with ESC) → NOT fence → `_formatMarkdownLine('...\x1b[2m``...')` → inline formatting of a line starting with ``` → probably unchanged (contains no ** etc.) → renders raw with the SGR.
2. `Goal.` — `_inFence` false → markdown line.
3. `'\x1b[2m```py\x1b[0m'`? No wait — in `_transcript`, only `p == '```'` lines get dim. ```py ` is NOT dim (comes from the summary content lines). Hmm wait: formatCompactionReport returns lines: 'summary:', '```', summary (multi-line string 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)'), '```'. In the test, each report line is split on '\n' and `p == '```'` gets dimed. So ```py ` is inside the summary string → stays raw.

Pre-fix with the unbalanced summary 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)':
1. outer ``` (dim) — no latch (bug).
2. `Goal.` — markdown (renders as plain, no indent — actually same visually since plain text renders as plain).
3. ```py ` (raw) — matches `_fenceRe` → `_inFence` toggles to TRUE → dim-wrap.
4. `print(1)` — in fence → ' print(1)' (indented).
5. outer closing ``` (dim) — hasMatch fails → NOT fence → markdown... `_inFence` stays TRUE.
6. 'Answer **after** compaction' — in fence → ' Answer **after** compaction' (verbatim, indented, raw `**`) — THE BUG: swallowed.
7. '# Heading after' — in fence → verbatim raw.

Post-fix:
1. outer ``` (dim) — stripped text '```' matches → latch IN, pass through verbatim.
2. `Goal.` — in fence → ' Goal.'.
3. ```py ` — raw matches → toggle OUT, dim-wrap.
4. `print(1)` — outside → markdown → plain 'print(1)'.
5. outer closing ``` (dim) — stripped matches → toggle IN, verbatim.
6. Hmm wait — that leaves _inFence TRUE... then:
7. 'Answer **after** compaction' — in fence?! 

Wait, I forgot `_balanceSummaryFences`! With balancing, the summary becomes 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)\n```' so line 4b is an appended raw ``` (not dim since it comes from the summary string... wait, the appended ``` is part of the summary string returned by formatCompactionReport — the test's map dims `p == '```'` → the appended fence line IS exactly '```' after split → dimed).

Post-fix sequence with balancing:
1. outer ``` (dim) → latch IN.
2. ' Goal.' (fence body).
3. ```py ` (raw) → toggle OUT (dim-wrapped).
4. 'print(1)' → markdown.
5. appended ``` (dim) → stripped matches → toggle IN, verbatim.
6. outer closing ``` (dim) → toggle OUT, verbatim.
7. 'Answer **after**...' → markdown with bold. ✓
8. '# Heading after' → markdown heading. ✓

Great, consistent with the AC3 golden. And AC1 checks pass.

Now — the deeper question I should double check: **is `_balanceSummaryFences` needed at all given the renderer fix?** Yes: without balancing, the summary's unbalanced fence leaves the toggle count odd: outer(1) + inner(1, latch) + outer-close(fails? no post-fix it latches)... post-fix without balancing: toggles = outer IN, ```py OUT, print(1) md, outer-close IN → answer swallowed INSIDE fence (indented verbatim). So yes, both changes are needed: renderer fix alone doesn't fix AC1 — the report-level balancing closes the gap. Actually wait, post-fix WITHOUT balancing: 1(outer) + 1(inner ```py) + 1(outer close) = 3 toggles = odd → ends IN fence. Correct, balancing is needed. And balancing alone (without renderer fix): the dimed outer fences still never latch... toggles seen: ```py (1) + appended ``` (2) → even → the outer dimed fences don't matter, ends OUT. Hmm interesting — balancing alone WOULD have fixed AC1's visible symptom (post-fix parity is what matters). But the renderer fix is needed for AC2-style correctness (styled fences latch and pass through byte-identically; also prevents `summary:` fence-body lines from being markdown-rendered). Both are justified; the test pins both.

Now, potential issue: **double-styling check in `_printCompactionReport`** — the printer dims `line == '```'` — with `_balanceSummaryFences`, the appended ``` is embedded IN the summary line, so the printer does NOT dim it (it's not a standalone line). The test compensates by diming after split. In the real TUI, how does the report land in the transcript? Let me check how `_printCompactionReport`'s output enters the TUI output history — does the TUI store the io.writeln output (with dim SGR baked in) line-by-line? Let me look at how the TUI captures io.writeln lines. Actually in the real CLI the report is printed via `io.writeln` — for TUI mode, is there a transcript-capturing io? Let me check briefly how the compaction report enters the TUI output history to confirm the test's `_transcript` simulates reality (dim on the exact-``` lines only).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1755-tui-fence` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +187
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T20:51:02Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:15:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #1755.

## What

The TUI transcript renderer (`TranscriptMarkdown`/`_formatFence`, lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart) regex-tested the RAW line for fence markers, so a fence line carrying ANSI SGR bytes — the compaction report dims its ``` lines at print time — failed `_fenceRe` (anchored `^````), the fence state never latched, and everything after an unbalanced fence rendered verbatim (raw `**`, `#` headings) instead of markdown.

## Attribution

Essence of the stranded working fix by Yury Bakhmutski on `fix/tui-compaction-summary-fence` (commit 7557efeeb, closed PR #1747) — re-landed here and adapted to the post-gh-1636 `formatCompactionReport` API. Cherry-pick credit: @YuryBY.

## Change

- **lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart** — `_formatFence(line, stripped)`: fence-test the ANSI-stripped text; a styled fence line toggles state and passes through byte-identically (no double-dim), plain fence lines still dim-wrap as before.
- **lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart** — `_balanceSummaryFences`: an odd fence count in the LLM summary gets a closing fence appended so the outer report fence cannot be left toggled open.
- **test/cli/tui_compaction_render_regression_test.dart** — the regression suite (adapted from 7557efeeb: `details: true` so the fenced summary actually renders post-gh-1636).

## AC coverage

- **AC1** — a summary ending mid-fence: rows after the report render as markdown (bold SGR present, no raw `**`/`#`) — pinned by "a summary with unbalanced ``` fences does not swallow the rows after it".
- **AC2** — styled fence lines still latch fences and pass through byte-identically (no double-dim); plain fence lines still dim-wrap — pinned by "styled fence lines still latch fences without double-styling (AC2)".
- **AC3** — balanced-fence transcripts byte-identical — pinned by two goldens (report-integration styled + plain literal renderer), each byte-captured from the live renderer.

## Gates (standalone Dart SDK 3.13.6 in-worktree; shared-box guard SIGKills system dart)

- `dart analyze` on the 3 touched files: no issues.
- `dart format` on the 3 touched files: clean.
- `dart test test/cli/tui_compaction_render_regression_test.dart`: 5/5 pass.
- Adjacent suites (ansi_markdown, compaction_report, transcript_answer_once, markdown_surface): 87/87 pass.
- AC3 byte-identity proven empirically, not just asserted: the plain REG golden passes UNCHANGED against the pre-fix renderer (507415794e), and the AC1 test FAILS on the pre-fix renderer (bug reproduced), then passes post-fix.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)

Alternative lighter check: reason from the code. Pre-fix `_formatFence(line)` tests raw line `\x1b[2m``` \x1b[0m` against `^\s*`` — ESC is not whitespace → no match → fence never latches → after the outer fence, subsequent lines render as markdown (wait, actually the pre-fix bug: outer dim fence doesn't latch IN, so `summary:` body lines render as markdown instead of verbatim, and the unbalanced inner ``` ` toggles... let me re-verify the exact mechanics:

Pre-fix, transcript lines:
1. `'\x1b[2m``` \x1b[0m'` (outer open, dim) — `_fenceRe.hasMatch(raw)` fails (starts with ESC) → NOT fence → `_formatMarkdownLine('...\x1b[2m``...')` → inline formatting of a line starting with ``` → probably unchanged (contains no ** etc.) → renders raw with the SGR.
2. `Goal.` — `_inFence` false → markdown line.
3. `'\x1b[2m```py\x1b[0m'`? No wait — in `_transcript`, only `p == '```'` lines get dim. ```py ` is NOT dim (comes from the summary content lines). Hmm wait: formatCompactionReport returns lines: 'summary:', '```', summary (multi-line string 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)'), '```'. In the test, each report line is split on '\n' and `p == '```'` gets dimed. So ```py ` is inside the summary string → stays raw.

Pre-fix with the unbalanced summary 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)':
1. outer ``` (dim) — no latch (bug).
2. `Goal.` — markdown (renders as plain, no indent — actually same visually since plain text renders as plain).
3. ```py ` (raw) — matches `_fenceRe` → `_inFence` toggles to TRUE → dim-wrap.
4. `print(1)` — in fence → ' print(1)' (indented).
5. outer closing ``` (dim) — hasMatch fails → NOT fence → markdown... `_inFence` stays TRUE.
6. 'Answer **after** compaction' — in fence → ' Answer **after** compaction' (verbatim, indented, raw `**`) — THE BUG: swallowed.
7. '# Heading after' — in fence → verbatim raw.

Post-fix:
1. outer ``` (dim) — stripped text '```' matches → latch IN, pass through verbatim.
2. `Goal.` — in fence → ' Goal.'.
3. ```py ` — raw matches → toggle OUT, dim-wrap.
4. `print(1)` — outside → markdown → plain 'print(1)'.
5. outer closing ``` (dim) — stripped matches → toggle IN, verbatim.
6. Hmm wait — that leaves _inFence TRUE... then:
7. 'Answer **after** compaction' — in fence?! 

Wait, I forgot `_balanceSummaryFences`! With balancing, the summary becomes 'Goal.\n```py\nprint(1)\n```' so line 4b is an appended raw ``` (not dim since it comes from the summary string... wait, the appended ``` is part of the summary string returned by formatCompactionReport — the test's map dims `p == '```'` → the appended fence line IS exactly '```' after split → dimed).

Post-fix sequence with balancing:
1. outer ``` (dim) → latch IN.
2. ' Goal.' (fence body).
3. ```py ` (raw) → toggle OUT (dim-wrapped).
4. 'print(1)' → markdown.
5. appended ``` (dim) → stripped matches → toggle IN, verbatim.
6. outer closing ``` (dim) → toggle OUT, verbatim.
7. 'Answer **after**...' → markdown with bold. ✓
8. '# Heading after' → markdown heading. ✓

Great, consistent with the AC3 golden. And AC1 checks pass.

Now — the deeper question I should double check: **is `_balanceSummaryFences` needed at all given the renderer fix?** Yes: without balancing, the summary's unbalanced fence leaves the toggle count odd: outer(1) + inner(1, latch) + outer-close(fails? no post-fix it latches)... post-fix without balancing: toggles = outer IN, ```py OUT, print(1) md, outer-close IN → answer swallowed INSIDE fence (indented verbatim). So yes, both changes are needed: renderer fix alone doesn't fix AC1 — the report-level balancing closes the gap. Actually wait, post-fix WITHOUT balancing: 1(outer) + 1(inner ```py) + 1(outer close) = 3 toggles = odd → ends IN fence. Correct, balancing is needed. And balancing alone (without renderer fix): the dimed outer fences still never latch... toggles seen: ```py (1) + appended ``` (2) → even → the outer dimed fences don't matter, ends OUT. Hmm interesting — balancing alone WOULD have fixed AC1's visible symptom (post-fix parity is what matters). But the renderer fix is needed for AC2-style correctness (styled fences latch and pass through byte-identically; also prevents `summary:` fence-body lines from being markdown-rendered). Both are justified; the test pins both.

Now, potential issue: **double-styling check in `_printCompactionReport`** — the printer dims `line == '```'` — with `_balanceSummaryFences`, the appended ``` is embedded IN the summary line, so the printer does NOT dim it (it's not a standalone line). This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.
